notes: Transcribed from SIR 2015-5019-F ver. 1.1 (February 2018), basin-characteristics equations only. Equations, n, model error variance (sigma_delta^2), MVP and SEP from Table 1-4 and covariance matrices [X^T Lambda^-1 X]^-1 from Table 1-5, both in sir20155019F_tables.xlsx (the PDF only lists the appendix tables); variable limits from Table 3 (report p. 12). Table 1-4 and Table 3 were double-entered (hand transcription vs. a regex parse of the workbook's equation strings and of pdftotext -table output): 696 cells, 0 disagreements; all 80 NSS equation strings (Montana, citation 88) carry the same coefficients. Regions and NSS codes: W GC1675, NW GC1768, NWF GC1677, NEP GC1678, ECP GC1679, SEP GC1680, UYCM GC1681, SW GC1682 (there is no GC1676 in NSS; the Northwest region is GC1768). Variables use NSS codes: CONTDA (report A, contributing drainage area, mi2; the drainage variable is CONTDA, not DRNAREA), PRECIP (P, in.), FOREST (F, percent), EL5000 and EL6000 (E5000, E6000, percent of basin above 5,000/6,000 ft), SLOP30_30M (SLP30, percent), ET0306MOD (ETSPR, mean March-June evapotranspiration, in. per month). Transforms: A, P and ETSPR log10; terms printed as (X + 1)^b use log10_plus1. Intercept = log10 of the printed coefficient. Units: model_error_variance and avp are Table 1-4's sigma_delta^2 and MVP (mean variance of prediction), log10 units squared, as printed. sep_log is Table 1-4's SEP (percent) converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10); SEM and pseudo/adjusted R2 are not stored. n_sites is Table 1-4's n, which is smaller for Q66.7 in several regions (Table 1-4 footnote 1). Covariance order and basis (intercept, then the variables in printed-equation order, all in the transformed basis) is confirmed two ways: the report's Case 1 worked example (p. 21, Southeast Plains Q1: x0 = [1, log A, log(F+1), log ETSPR], x0'Ux0 = 0.00924) and, for every region and AEP, MEV + mean x'Ux over the region's gages in Table 1-3 reproduces Table 1-4's MVP within 0.0013 (MVP is printed to 3 decimals). The Northwest region was fit by weighted least squares, not GLS (ver. 1.1 changed it; Table 1-4 footnote 3, Table 1-5 footnote 2): its model error variance is printed 0.000 for Q4 through Q0.2 and is stored as 0.0, so its site-specific prediction variance is x'Ux alone; its covariance entries are printed to fewer digits than the GLS regions'. Report inconsistency (not in this file): the Case 3 example (p. 24) evaluates the East-Central Plains Q2 equation with a = 433, but Table 1-4 and NSS give 497; Table 1-4 is used. Out of scope: the channel-width equations of Chase and others (SIR 2020-5142; NSS citation 163, 24 regions GC1829-GC1852) are a separate method, combined with basin-characteristics estimates by SEP and cross-correlation weighting that evaluate_weighted does not model; they are not included.
